## A note on Makefile and Taskfile alternatives

Not everyone searching for “make alternatives” is looking at Make.com. The `make` build tool and its `Makefile` syntax remain widely used for compiling code and running project tasks, but their tab-sensitive syntax, limited cross-platform behavior, and awkward handling of anything beyond file targets push many teams to look elsewhere.

For task running and builds, the common Makefile alternatives are Task (which uses a readable YAML `Taskfile.yml`), Just (a command runner with a cleaner syntax than `make`), and language-native tools like `npm` scripts, Gradle, or Bazel. These are the right fit when your goal is local builds and developer task running. [...] October 2 2026

# Best Make Alternatives and Competitors(2026)

The best Make alternatives

Make (formerly Integromat) is the visual automation builder people move to when Zapier gets expensive. The free plan gives you 1,000 credits a month and 2 active scenarios. Paid plans start at $12 a month for 10,000 credits, and Pro and Teams run $21 and $38.

It's cheaper than Zapier, but it's still a meter. Complex scenarios with loops and error handling burn credits quickly, and the visual builder has a real learning curve. Some people want the same automations with AI building them from a sentence.

Before you switch, look at your busiest scenario and how many credits it uses a month. Check the alternative supports the same apps and webhooks, and how it charges when a scenario runs a lot.
